text: {"question":"How do the recent deuterium observations influence the disagreement between baryon density estimates from deuterium and the CMB within the standard cosmological model, and how does this compare to the broader conclusion that systematic errors are unlikely to resolve the Hubble constant discrepancy?","reference_answer":"Recent deuterium data reduce the conflict between the baryon density inferred from D/H and that from the CMB by about one standard deviation, even in ΛCDM, while the wider body of work on diverse Hubble constant determinations suggests that systematic biases alone cannot explain the persistent H0 tension."}
